title: After Studying Abroad at the Medical University of Gdansk
paragraphs: I was allowed to do clerkships for three months at the Medical University of Gdansk in Poland.

[About the Medical University of Gdansk] The Medical University of Gdansk has two courses, the Polish Division and the English Division. The former is for Poles and provides medical education in Polish. The latter gathers students from all over the world and provides medical education in English. The students of the English Division come from a wide range of countries, such as Sweden, Saudi Arabia, India, Kenya and the United States. It was very fresh to do clerkships with students whose native languages, religions and skin colors differ and to communicate in English. At lunchtime there was one person who was eating nothing, so I asked, "Aren't you having lunch?", and I was surprised when the answer came back, "It's Ramadan, so I'm fasting."

[About the Clerkships] Together with the English Division students, I rotated in units of one to three weeks through internal medicine (diabetes, hypertension), obstetrics and gynecology, pediatrics, family medicine, surgery and pediatric surgery. Because it is formally incorporated into the English Division curriculum, I had to take a written or oral examination on the last day of each department or at the end of the semester. Since I do not even have sufficient knowledge in Japanese, taking examinations in English was quite hard. In the surgery clerkship we had lectures on gastrointestinal diseases, training in suturing and ligation, and observation of operations. In a group of about 20, there were only about five operations in which one could enter the sterile field, but I was fortunate to be able to take part in an appendectomy in a gown. Because I aspire to surgery, taking part in an operation overseas was one of my goals in studying abroad, so I am glad I achieved it. On the last day there was also a presentation contest. Presenting, nervously, on pancreaticoduodenectomy with Alex from Sweden is a good memory.

[Life in Gdansk] Prices are very cheap (a bottle of beer is 60 yen, 750 ml of milk is 60 yen and so on), and it is safe. It is the third tourist destination in Poland, and the streets of the old town are very beautiful, and I took photos of them again and again. In the three months I stayed in Gdansk I also made friends with whom I drank beer, ran and did strength training, and I was able to spend very fulfilling days. In addition, through an introduction from a senior who studied abroad last year, I joined a team called Ogniwo Sopot and was able to play rugby. I was even able to play in an official 7s match and was given the praise "You are a soldier," which became an unforgettable memory.

[After the Study Abroad] Finally, I sincerely thank everyone at the International Collaboration Office, starting with Dr. 粕谷 and Dr. 長谷川, who gave me such a valuable opportunity, the people at Academic Affairs, starting with Ms. 西尾, the members of the Gdansk group who held a send-off party for me, Professor Wozniak and Adam, who looked after me in various ways on site, and my roommate 川口, with whom I shared joys and hardships for three months. Thank you very much. It became the best three months of my life.
